paths.title: Christmas: Born in the City of David

nodes.label: Jesus Christ
nodes.summary: The son of David, the son of Abraham; the center every thread points to.

quote.text: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
he shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.
in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed

nodes.label: The Scepter of Judah
nodes.summary: The scepter shall not depart from Judah.

nodes.label: The Root of Jesse
nodes.summary: A shoot from the stump of Jesse, David's father.

nodes.label: Covenant with David
nodes.summary: God promises David an offspring whose throne and kingdom He will establish forever.

quote.text: Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

But you, O Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are too little to be among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel

nodes.label: Joseph

quote.text: the Lord God will give to him the throne of his father David

nodes.label: I Am the Bread of Life

edges.note: God sent forth his Son, born of woman. Many read Genesis 3:15 as the first gospel (protoevangelium); Romans 16:20 echoes the crushing of Satan.
The promised offspring narrows to Abraham's line. Widely held in Reformed covenant theology, but the Genesis text does not state the connection.
Paul: 'And to your offspring, who is Christ.'
The Lion of the tribe of Judah; our Lord descended from Judah.
Legal father, not biological; Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:20).
Matthew quotes Isaiah 9:1-2 of Jesus' ministry in Galilee. Applying 9:6-7 to Christ follows from this and from Luke 1:32-33.
The chief priests and scribes cite Micah 5:2 to Herod.
'Where is he who has been born king of the Jews?'
'House of bread' as a picture of the Bread of Life is devotional wordplay. Scripture never makes this link, so present it as illustration only.
